feature.description: A function that accesses a 24-bit unsigned bitfield from a struct and uses it in an arithmetic operation (e.g., multiplication), with the result assigned to a global int. This shape is necessary to generate the shift+mask+add RTL sequence that triggered the bug.
feature.root_cause_link: The 24-bit bitfield is zero-extended to 32 bits, then sign-extended to 64 bits, and the multiplication by 37 is decomposed into shifts and adds, creating the shift+mask pattern that late_combine tried to merge.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In the LoongArch backend, loongarch_reassoc_shift_bitwise() was called with SImode while the constant mask operand was actually DImode, causing a wide-int mode mismatch and ICE in late_combine when trying to combine a shift+mask pattern with an addition for the alsl.w instruction.

feature.description: Target backends providing mem_shadd_or_shadd_rtx_p must verify that the operand to be shifted (typically an index) is a register; otherwise a memory operand may be used in a shift, causing an unrecognizable insn.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The RISC-V/LoongArch backend function mem_shadd_or_shadd_rtx_p did not validate that the shifted operand was a register, allowing an ashift of a memory load when -ftree-ter was forced at -O0, causing an unrecognizable insn ICE in the vregs pass.

feature.description: On LoongArch64, when expanding SImode arithmetic or shift operations, if a temporary pseudo register is needed to perform the operation in DImode and then truncate, the expansion must check can_create_pseudo_p() to avoid creating a pseudo after reload.
feature.root_cause_link: Expansion unconditionally calls gen_reg_rtx, which fails after reload because pseudos cannot be created.

source_features.root_cause_summary: On LoongArch64, SImode arithmetic and shift expansions create a DImode pseudo to reduce sign extensions, but they lack can_create_pseudo_p() checks, causing ICE when expanded after reload during peephole2.

group_summary: Combines three LoongArch bugs into one executable test: sibcall target register clobber by epilogue (106096), FP ABI macro misdetection leading to wrong argument passing (109000), and padding-induced branch overflow (112330). The caller performs a tail call to the callee via a function pointer forced into $r13, includes padding before the call, and passes a double argument. The callee expects the double in integer registers (correct for -mabi=lp64s). Mismatch or clobber leads to wrong result.

feature.description: The register used as the target of a sibling call (sibcall) must not be clobbered by the epilogue of the calling function; if the target architecture uses a temporary register in the epilogue, that register must be excluded from the set of registers available for sibcall targets.
feature.root_cause_link: The epilogue clobbers $r13, so using it for sibcall target leads to jumping to a corrupted address.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch epilogue uses $r13 as a temporary register (LARCH_PROLOGUE_TEMP), but $r13 was included in SIBCALL_REGS, allowing it to be allocated for sibling call targets. When a sibcall was followed by the epilogue, the target address in $r13 was clobbered, causing a jump to an invalid address.

feature.description: In the LoongArch backend, the macros FP_RETURN and UNITS_PER_FP_ARG used TARGET_HARD_FLOAT, TARGET_SOFT_FLOAT, TARGET_DOUBLE_FLOAT (controlled by -mfpu) to determine FP calling convention, instead of the correct TARGET_HARD_FLOAT_ABI, TARGET_SOFT_FLOAT_ABI, TARGET_DOUBLE_FLOAT_ABI (controlled by -mabi).
feature.root_cause_link: This is the direct root cause: misuse of TARGET_*_FLOAT macros.

source_features.root_cause_summary: GCC LoongArch backend used TARGET_HARD_FLOAT etc. (affected by -mfpu) to determine FP calling convention, instead of TARGET_HARD_FLOAT_ABI (set by -mabi), causing ABI violation when -mfpu=64 with -mabi=lp64s.

feature.description: In the LoongArch backend, the macros FP_RETURN and UNITS_PER_FP_ARG used TARGET_HARD_FLOAT, TARGET_SOFT_FLOAT, TARGET_DOUBLE_FLOAT (controlled by -mfpu) to determine FP calling convention, instead of the correct TARGET_HARD_FLOAT_ABI, TARGET_SOFT_FLOAT_ABI, TARGET_DOUBLE_FLOAT_ABI (controlled by -mabi).

Global variable must have section attribute ".data.rel.ro" exactly.
The loop must use signed short to int widening to trigger even/odd multiply patterns; avoid using floating-point.
Stack buffer size must be large enough to trigger stack protector (>=8 bytes).
notes: All source features are preserved as invariants. The test generates one object file and runs two oracles (compilation success and assembly checks). The dependencies are satisfied by glue features G1 (source code) and G2 (check script).

must_not_change: Do not rewrite the loop to avoid vectorization; ensure -mlsx is used.
preservation_plan.placement: Function with a loop that performs widening multiplication of signed shorts and accumulates results into an int. This should trigger the vectorizer to emit vmulwev/vmulwod when -mlsx is enabled.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Target must have ISA support for LSX even/odd widening multiply (e.g., vmulwev/vmulwod). The test must trigger vectorizer to use these patterns.

must_not_change: Do not modify -mabi=lp64s; the check must be performed on the object file.
preservation_plan.placement: Post-compilation check: run readelf and objdump on the .o file to verify flags and instruction patterns.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Generated object file must have SOFT-FLOAT ELF flag and contain no FPR instructions (e.g., frecip, fmov, fadd).

must_not_change: Do not remove the canary check; ensure -fstack-protector-all is used.
preservation_plan.placement: Disassembly check: after the bne and before jr, ensure that the register used for canary (typically $r12) is not used again (e.g., no subsequent load or use).
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Stack canary value must not be live in a register at function return. After the canary check, the register holding the canary must be dead before jr $r1.

must_not_change: Do not change the section attribute; ensure -fPIC is used.
preservation_plan.placement: Source file includes a global variable with attribute section(".data.rel.ro"). The compilation must complete without ICE.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: No ICE from section type conflict when placing label addresses into .data.rel.ro with -fPIC. The compilation must succeed without internal error.

recommended_oracles: Compilation succeeds without ICE (bug-116887).
readelf shows SOFT-FLOAT flag (bug-109000).
objdump disassembly contains no FPR instructions (bug-109000).
Stack canary register is not used after the return jump (bug-125049).

semantic_risks.risk: Undefined behavior: if the widening multiply loop writes out of bounds, or if section attribute conflicts with target's default linker script.

feature.description: The target must have ISA support for even/odd widening multiply (e.g., LoongArch LSX vmulwev/vmulwod, x86 AVX/AVX512).
feature.root_cause_link: The vectorizer could not use these patterns due to the incorrect checks, so enabling even/odd operations requires both correct generic code and target patterns.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The vectorizer's supportable_widening_operation had an incorrect and redundant check (STMT_VINFO_RELEVANT == vect_used_by_reduction) that prevented use of even/odd widening multiply patterns for reductions, and a second check used the pattern statement instead of the original statement when looking for single use.

group_summary: Combine three independent LoongArch bugs into one test: (1) sibcall target clobbered by epilogue, (2) return value overwritten by EH register restore, (3) soft-float ABI violation. The test is a single assembly program that triggers both wrong-code bugs and checks the ELF flags and disassembly for soft-float compliance.
group_title: LoongArch epilogue register interference with sibcall and EH return under soft-float ABI
instantiation_constraints: All assembly code must be LoongArch64 compatible.
Must be assembled with -mabi=lp64s
Must link without soft-float runtime (no FP emulation libraries that use FP registers)
The sibcall bug requires optimization (-O2) to enable sibcall transformation
The EH bug requires that the compiler actually generates the epilogue restore (likely -O2 as well)
The test program must not use any floating-point data types or operations in source (or asm) to avoid soft-float violation
notes: The group combines three LoongArch bugs into a single assembly test. The glue functions provide the necessary orchestration. The primary risk is that the sibcall and EH bugs may not both trigger in the same compilation unit due to optimization; however, they are placed in separate functions to ensure isolation. The soft-float oracle checks the entire object file.

preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Register $r13 used as sibling call target must not be clobbered by epilogue (which uses $r13 as LARCH_PROLOGUE_TEMP).

preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: On normal return, epilogue restores EH_RETURN_DATA_REGNO registers ($r4-$r7) from stack, overwriting the return value in $r4.

must_not_change: Must not use -mfpu=64 or any -mfpu option that enables FP registers
The test code must not contain any floating-point loads/stores or operations
preservation_plan.placement: The entire test file must be compiled with -mabi=lp64s; the generated object file must be checked for SOFT-FLOAT flag and absence of FP instructions.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Soft-float ABI object must have SOFT-FLOAT ELF flag and must not contain any floating-point instructions.

recommended_oracles: Execute the program and check that it does not crash (for sibcall bug, possible crash; for EH bug, incorrect return value). More specifically, check that test_func_eh returns the expected value (not overwritten) and that test_func_sibcall correctly transfers control to target_func (e.g., by checking side effects).
After compilation, readelf -h <object> | grep Flags should show SOFT-FLOAT.
objdump -d <object> | grep -E 'frecip\.|fmov\.|fadd\.|fsub\.|fmul\.|fdiv\.' should be empty (no FP instructions).

semantic_risks.risk: The EH bug requires that the compiler actually restores $r4-$r7 on a normal return; if the function is small and the compiler elides the restore, the bug doesn't appear.

semantic_risks.risk: Soft-float ABI might conflict with use of $r4 for return value if the compiler uses floating-point registers for something else.

feature.description: The register used as the target of a sibling call (sibcall) must not be clobbered by the epilogue of the calling function; if the target architecture uses a temporary register in the epilogue, that register must be excluded from the set of registers available for sibcall targets.
feature.root_cause_link: The epilogue clobbers $r13, so using it for sibcall target leads to jumping to a corrupted address.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch epilogue uses $r13 as a temporary register (LARCH_PROLOGUE_TEMP), but $r13 was included in SIBCALL_REGS, allowing it to be allocated for sibling call targets. When a sibcall was followed by the epilogue, the target address in $r13 was clobbered, causing a jump to an invalid address.

feature.description: LoongArch target where EH_RETURN_DATA_REGN registers $r4-$r7 are also used for function return values; the epilogue restore of these registers from the stack on a normal return path causes the return value to be overwritten.
feature.root_cause_link: The LoongArch backend always restored eh_return data registers in epilogue, and $r4 is both a return register and an eh_return data register.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch epilogue unconditionally restored EH_RETURN_DATA_REGNO registers ($r4-$r7) on normal return paths, overwriting the function return value.

group_summary: Combines five LoongArch assembly pattern features into a single C function that, when compiled with -O2 -fsignaling-nans -march=loongarch64, generates all expected instructions: fclass.s for isnan, maskeqz for conditional select, bytepick for bitfield combine, sltu+slli+add for conditional power-of-two add, and fcopysign.d for copysign(x,-1).
group_title: LoongArch instruction selection integration with signaling NaNs
instantiation_constraints: Function 'test' must be compiled as C (not C++) to avoid mangling issues.
Must include builtins: __builtin_isnan, __builtin_copysign.
Do not use -fno-builtin-* flags.
Inputs must be non-NaN for copysign and bytepick to produce defined behavior; isnan should be called on a possible sNaN, but -fsignaling-nans ensures no exception.
notes: All five features are LoongArch assembly pattern checks. They are combined via data flow in a single C function. The glue features provide type punning, volatile sinks, and bitfield macros. Compiler with -O2 -fsignaling-nans -march=loongarch64 should produce all patterns.

must_not_change: Do not use -fno-signaling-nans or change the builtin.
preservation_plan.placement: In function 'test', call to __builtin_isnan(x) with -fsignaling-nans flag.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Assembly must contain fclass.s, movfr2gr.s, andi, sltu sequence for isnan expansion, avoiding fcmp.cun.s.

must_not_change: cond must be of integer type, not bool, to avoid elimination.
a must be an integer variable.
preservation_plan.placement: In function 'test', compute 'int sel = a * cond;' where cond is boolean from isnan.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Assembly must contain maskeqz instruction for the expression 'a * (cond != 0)', and must NOT contain mul instruction in that context.

must_not_change: The two operands must have non-overlapping bits.
Combine operator must be one of |, ^, +.
preservation_plan.placement: In function 'test', compute 'uint64_t c = (a & 0xFFFF) | ((b & 0xFFFF0000) >> 16);' but ensure that the combine operator is OR/PLUS/XOR; use a macro that expands to a compound expression that GCC may match.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Assembly must contain bytepick.d instruction combining two non-overlapping bitfields using an OR (or PLUS/XOR) operation.

must_not_change: Constant must be a power of two (1<<16).
Condition must be a store flag from sltu (i.e., compare producing 0/1).
preservation_plan.placement: In function 'test', compute 'y += (cond ? 0x10000 : 0);' where y is an integer variable.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Assembly must contain sltu, slli, add sequence for conditional addition of constant power of two (here 1<<16).

must_not_change: Second argument must be a negative constant (-1.0).
Target must have native copysign instruction (LoongArch).
preservation_plan.placement: In function 'test', call '__builtin_copysign(x, -1.0)' (or copysign from math.h with -fno-builtin-copysign? actually use __builtin_copysign).
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Assembly must contain fcopysign.d instruction for copysign(x, -1.0) and must NOT contain fabs.d followed by fneg.d.

recommended_oracles: Scan assembly for fclass.s, movfr2gr.s, andi, sltu (in that order).
Scan assembly for maskeqz instruction (not mul).
Scan assembly for bytepick.d instruction.
Scan assembly for sltu, slli.d, add.d sequence with immediate 16.
Scan assembly for fcopysign.d (not fabs.d nor fneg.d).
Verify that total number of assembly lines is reasonable (no infinite loop).

semantic_risks.risk: If -fsignaling-nans is not supported on this LoongArch variant, __builtin_isnan may trap or expand differently.

semantic_risks.risk: The conditional add pattern requires the condition to be a store-flag (0/1). If the compiler transforms the boolean differently, the sltu+slli+add might not appear.

feature.description: LoongArch bytepick.d instruction can combine two non-overlapping bitfields from two 64-bit words into one, requiring a pattern that accepts IOR, XOR, or PLUS.
feature.root_cause_link: Fix added any_or_plus iterator to bytepick patterns to match PLUS and XOR produced after r15-1120.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Middle-end change r15-1120 started using PLUS instead of IOR for combining non-overlapping bitfields, but target patterns (aarch64 extr, LoongArch bytepick) only matched IOR, causing missed optimizations. Fixed by adding a code iterator (any_or_plus) to accept IOR, XOR, and PLUS in the affected patterns.

feature.description: On LoongArch, conditional add by a constant power of two should use a shifted store flag sequence (set condition, shift, add) rather than a mask-based conditional zero sequence, matching the target's preferred code generation.
feature.root_cause_link: The initial fix for PR125731 introduced a regression on LoongArch by generating conditional-zero masks; LoongArch prefers sltu+slli+add for such cases.

source_features.root_cause_summary: ifcvt.cc failed to generate conditional zero sequences when one operand is a CONST_INT, and lacked optimization for selects across A and A OP C where C is a power of two.

feature.description: On targets with native copysign, compiling copysign(x, -1.0) at -O2 should generate a direct copysign instruction rather than a sequence of fabs and fneg. Using simplify_unary_operation avoids forcing an early expansion that could mask further folding.
mutation_knobs: instruction pattern: scan for fcopysign vs fabs+fneg
feature.root_cause_link: The second fix (commit 9e9279f) addressed a de-optimization where copysign was expanded to fneg(fabs) even when a native copysign existed. Using simplify_unary_operation allows the ABS to be folded before generating NEG, preserving the copysign opportunity.

feature.description: On LoongArch64 (and other 64-bit architectures where pointers may have non-zero upper 32 bits after writing a 32-bit zero), writing an int value of 0 to a union member and later reading the storage as a pointer does not necessarily yield a null pointer. This exposes undefined behavior when code relies on such type-punning to produce a null pointer.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Union type-punning in the COBOL front end: assigning to an int member and reading as a char* member produced a non-null garbage pointer on LoongArch64, causing a spurious dialect warning and test failures. Fix: removed the type-punning assignment, properly set the pointer to NULL, and added trailing context to the lexer keyword pattern.

feature.description: A code shape containing a switch statement with many dense case labels, which tends to be compiled into a jump table, potentially using an indirect jump instruction.
feature.root_cause_link: With old constraints, regrename could use $ra for the jump table's indirect jump; with new constraints, it won't.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Micro-architecture unconditionally treats 'jr $ra' as a return, causing branch prediction interference when $ra is used for non-return indirect jumps; fix was to restrict jump table and indirect jump patterns from using $ra via constraint 'e'.

feature.description: When targeting LoongArch with LSX or LASX enabled, vector integer types of width 128 or 256 bits will be lowered to LSX/LASX instructions after the removal of vcond expanders relies on the vec_cmp and vcond_mask patterns.
feature.root_cause_link: Commit 0498f8bda1d08b8ed8100d759917792baf2da15f removed vcond{,u} expanders from LoongArch backend; new code must use vec_cmp and vcond_mask. This test exercises those paths.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Target backends still contain obsolete vcond, vcondu, vcondeq expanders; the modern approach uses vec_cmp{,u,eq} plus vcond_mask. Removal of these legacy optabs and corresponding match.pd optimization ensures correctness and future-proofing.

feature.description: A define_insn_and_split pattern for a bit-clear operation (AND with a zero-bitmask constant) must prevent memory destinations via output constraint, otherwise the compiler may ICE when splitting the insn during final.
feature.root_cause_link: Missing '=r' constraint on output operand of bstrins_<mode>_for_mask caused splitter to accept memory target, leading to ICE.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Missing constraints in LoongArch bstrins_<mode>_for_mask and bstrins_<mode>_for_ior_mask define_insn_and_split patterns allowed memory operands that could not be split, causing an ICE during final.

feature.description: Compiling LoongArch PIC code with a static variable in .data.rel.ro section and an address comparison involving a global symbol's address triggers a section type conflict ICE.
mutation_knobs: size of the buffer in rtld_global (affects offset of _dl_rtld_map)
static vs non-static for the variable
feature.root_cause_link: The lack of proper section flags for .data.rel.ro in LoongArch backend, combined with cost model decisions, leads to conflicting section flags when the constant pool entry is placed in the same section.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch backend did not properly handle section attributes for .data.rel.ro when placing constant pool entries into that section, causing a section type conflict due to mismatched flags. The fix adjusts the cost model to avoid forcing label addresses into the constant pool, thereby preventing the conflict.

source_features.root_cause_summary: loongarch_expand_vec_perm_1 incorrectly handled shuffle indices for xvshuf.* instructions when the mask contained out-of-range elements, leading to unpredictable hardware behavior and wrong code. The fix simplified the masking logic to properly wrap or mask indices.

feature.description: The ICE manifests during RTL scheduler initialization (sched1 pass) when IRA computes register costs by scanning instructions with vector floating-point AND/IOR patterns and checking constraint YC.
mutation_knobs: change -O3 to -O2 might not trigger because sched1 not invoked
feature.root_cause_link: The bug is exposed when the scheduler queries IRA for register costs, which triggers YC constraint checking on the AND/IOR pattern.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch backend functions loongarch_const_vector_bitimm_set_p/clr_p and loongarch_const_vector_same_bytes_p did not handle floating-point vector modes, causing an ICE when vector float constants were used as bitwise immediate operands (constraint YC) in AND/IOR patterns generated from copysign vector operations.

feature.description: The LoongArch64 target with -O3 (or -O2) optimization, which enables the scheduler (sched1) and the CRC combining pattern, is required for the ICE.
feature.root_cause_link: The target-specific CRC pattern and scheduler are necessary for the nested subreg issue.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch crc_combine define_insn_and_split created a nested subreg (subreg of subreg) because register_operand can match a subreg, causing an unrecognizable insn ICE in sched1. Fixed by replacing the explicit subreg with lowpart_subreg.

feature.description: Offset of a field within a large struct (beyond 12-bit immediate) influences whether the backend places its address into the constant pool, potentially triggering a section conflict with .data.rel.ro on LoongArch PIC.
mutation_knobs: size of padding before the field
whether the field is accessed directly or via pointer
feature.root_cause_link: The fix changed the cost calculation to avoid forcing constant memory for large offsets, preventing the address from being placed in .data.rel.ro inadvertently.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch backend did not properly handle section attributes for .data.rel.ro when placing constant pool entries into that section, causing a section type conflict due to mismatched flags. The fix adjusts the cost model to avoid forcing label addresses into the constant pool, thereby preventing the conflict.

feature.description: On LoongArch64, objects containing R_LARCH_B26 relocations (e.g., function calls) must be compiled with -mcmodel=extreme when the final linked text segment can exceed 128MB, to ensure the relocation offset fits within the allowed range.
feature.root_cause_link: Default code model for crtbeginS.o was insufficient for large code segments, fixed by using -mcmodel=extreme.

source_features.root_cause_summary: On LoongArch64, the default code model for crtbeginS.o allowed R_LARCH_B26 relocations with a limited range, causing out-of-range errors when the total text segment size exceeded 128MB and lld linker placed crtbeginS.o before the .text section; fixed by using -mcmodel=extreme for crtbeginS.o.

feature.description: The false positive manifests on arm-none-eabi and loongarch64-linux-gnu targets, presumably due to their vectorization capabilities and ABI conventions for array accesses.
feature.root_cause_link: The vectorizer/loop optimizer behavior is influenced by the target's cost model and vector ISAs, which determine peeling and epilogue generation.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Tree vectorizer generates a scalar epilogue loop that appears to write beyond the destination array to the array-bound-check heuristics, causing a false positive -Wstringop-overflow warning.

feature.description: The cost factor for ADDRESS_REG_REG in loongarch_address_insns can be varied (e.g., factor*1, factor*2, factor*3, factor*4) to study impact on performance and code generation.
feature.root_cause_link: Tentative fix changes this factor from 1 to 3, which partially recovers performance. The optimal value may depend on microarchitecture.

source_features.root_cause_summary: A change in SCEV chrec_fold_multiply (commit e0e9499aeffd) altered loop analysis, causing suboptimal address selection on LoongArch. The RTL address cost for register+register addressing (ADDRESS_REG_REG) was too low (factor), leading to excessive complex addressing that increased register pressure and code size, degrading performance. Tentative fix increased cost to factor*3.

feature.description: When the compiler supports __float128 as an alias for _Float128, floating-point constants with a Q suffix must be accepted and interpreted as __float128.
mutation_knobs: use in initializer, assignment, or return context
feature.root_cause_link: LoongArch backend did not implement TARGET_C_MODE_FOR_SUFFIX for Q suffix, causing the frontend to reject the constant.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch lacked TARGET_C_MODE_FOR_SUFFIX handling for 'Q'/'q' suffixes, causing rejection of valid __float128 constants. Additionally, enabling __float128 support inadvertently caused libquadmath to be linked on LoongArch, where long double is already IEEE quad, leading to Fortran link failures; fixed by disabling __float128 support in libgfortran and libquadmath on LoongArch.

feature.description: The use of __builtin_memcpy with a size of 4 bytes to transfer bits between float and int types forces the compiler to treat the value as a bit pattern; varying the size and the types can expose whether the move instruction targets a floating-point or integer register and whether sign-extension is applied.
feature.root_cause_link: The builtin_memcpy introduces the move operation that triggers the sign-extension redundancy.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The compiler failed to recognize that LoongArch's movfr2gr.s already sign-extends a 32-bit value moved from a floating-point register to a 64-bit general-purpose register, causing a redundant slli.w instruction to be emitted.

feature.description: The IRA register pressure computation must not overestimate pressure due to target rtx costs, leading to excessive spilling and poor scheduling on LA664. The pressure classes should explicitly include GENERAL_REGS, FP_REGS, and FCC_REGS.
feature.root_cause_link: The fix defines TARGET_COMPUTE_PRESSURE_CLASSES to override the default automatic calculation that was influenced by rtx costs.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The rtx cost values defined by the LoongArch target backend influenced the default IRA register pressure class calculation, leading to poor scheduling decisions and performance degradation on LA664 cores. The fix provides explicit pressure classes (GENERAL_REGS, FP_REGS, FCC_REGS) to avoid the automatic calculation.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In the LoongArch backend, loongarch_reassoc_shift_bitwise() was called with SImode while the constant mask operand was actually DImode, causing a wide-int mode mismatch and ICE in late_combine when trying to combine a shift+mask pattern with an addition for the alsl.w instruction.

feature.description: On LoongArch 64-bit, the 32-bit division/modulo instruction (div.w[u], mod.w[u]) requires its inputs to be properly sign-extended or zero-extended 32-bit values; a DI-mode operand with undefined upper 32 bits leads to unspecified behavior and can expose compiler internal errors.

feature.description: Excessive DFA multipass scheduling lookahead on out-of-order LoongArch64 processors (e.g., LA664) causes massive compile-time explosions, especially for large loop-heavy translation units with many independent operations, because the scheduler explores too many ready-queue permutations without proportional performance gain on OoO hardware.
feature.root_cause_link: The TARGET_SCHED_FIRST_CYCLE_MULTIPASS_DFA_LOOKAHEAD value was raised from 4 to 6 for LA664, causing the DFA scheduler to spend excessive time in the sched2 pass; the proposed fix reduces it to 0 for all 64-bit tunings.

source_features.root_cause_summary: TARGET_SCHED_FIRST_CYCLE_MULTIPASS_DFA_LOOKAHEAD set to 6 for LA664 tuning causes exponential compile-time explosion on large out-of-order LoongArch64 cores due to excessive multipass scheduling permutations.

feature.code_witness: /* In config/loongarch/loongarch.h */ #define LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT 0
feature.description: The target macro LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT, when defined to 0, instructs the compiler to avoid non-short-circuit evaluation of logical operations, which can be beneficial if conditional sets are expensive. For LoongArch, it is currently set to 0 for fast-math, but this has performance implications for integer code as well.
feature.root_cause_link: The bug was about this macro being incorrectly set for RISC-V; LoongArch's setting may need similar investigation.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The RISC-V port incorrectly defined LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT=0, likely inherited from MIPS, causing missed optimizations for logical expressions with cheap conditional sets; fixed by removing the macro to use the default.

feature.description: When compiling a subword atomic exchange on LoongArch, the generated assembly should contain only a single branch instruction (beq or bne) for the compare-and-loop portion; a second branch indicates the fallback path from a failed compare, which is incorrect for exchange because the store must always occur.
feature.root_cause_link: The old expansion had two branches: one for the compare failure and one for the loop back-edge; the correct expansion only needs one back-edge branch. So scanning for 1 branch detects the bug.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch backend expanded subword atomic_exchange into an incorrect load-cmpxchg sequence where the store could be skipped due to a concurrent write, fixed by introducing a dedicated exchange pattern that always completes the store.

feature.description: When -mstrict-align is used on LoongArch, memcpy with unaligned source/destination (e.g., char pointers) should not generate a long straight-line byte-copy sequence; instead, it should use a loop to reduce code size.
feature.root_cause_link: The original expansion limited straight-line by byte count, causing too many instructions for unaligned strict-align case; fix limits by instruction count and uses loop.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch cpymemsi expansion generated inefficient inline code for memcpy of certain sizes under -mno-strict-align because it did not use wider modes when unaligned access was allowed, and improperly handled remainders by falling back to byte transfers. The fix improves alignment handling and uses a mode-halving strategy for leftovers.

feature.root_cause_link: Select TLS descriptor dialect influences relaxation paths; linker bug surfaces with -mtls-dialect=desc.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch linker incorrectly performed TLS descriptor to initial exec relaxation without updating the instruction sequence, causing a crash when -fPIC and -mtls-dialect=desc were used.

feature.description: To detect the performance regression, scan the assembly output for LoongArch's jr instruction with $r1 (the return address register) that is not part of a subroutine return; any such occurrence indicates a potential branch prediction penalty.
feature.root_cause_link: The fix excludes $ra from jumptable/indirect_jump patterns, so any jr $r1 for those patterns is a bug.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Micro-architecture unconditionally treats 'jr $ra' as a return, causing branch prediction interference when $ra is used for non-return indirect jumps; fix was to restrict jump table and indirect jump patterns from using $ra via constraint 'e'.

feature.code_witness: fp_add (COSTS_N_INSNS (5)), fp_mult_sf (COSTS_N_INSNS (5)), int_mult_si (COSTS_N_INSNS (4)),
feature.description: The cost model in loongarch_rtx_cost_data affects combine decisions; incorrectly low multiplication costs prevent substitution of shift-add instructions.
mutation_knobs: vary cost values to test sensitivity
feature.root_cause_link: The constructor with old costs directly caused the missed optimisation; the fix updates those values.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Incorrect instruction cost model in loongarch_rtx_cost_data caused the compiler to prefer direct multiply instructions over shift-add sequences for constant multiplication on LoongArch, missing optimizations because the mul cost was set too low; the fix adjusted costs based on micro-benchmarks.

feature.code_witness: /* Expected behavior: with factor*3, fewer reg+reg addresses generated, leading to more spill code but better overall performance. */
feature.description: For LoongArch, using too many register+register addressing modes in tight loops can increase register pressure and degrade performance. The cost model should discourage excessive ADDRESS_REG_REG usage when it leads to spilling.
feature.root_cause_link: The regression is due to underestimating cost; the invariant is that a correct cost model prevents the compiler from choosing too many complex addresses.

source_features.root_cause_summary: A change in SCEV chrec_fold_multiply (commit e0e9499aeffd) altered loop analysis, causing suboptimal address selection on LoongArch. The RTL address cost for register+register addressing (ADDRESS_REG_REG) was too low (factor), leading to excessive complex addressing that increased register pressure and code size, degrading performance. Tentative fix increased cost to factor*3.

feature.description: On LoongArch, #pragma GCC target("tune=...") must update the predefined macro __loongarch_tune to reflect the new tune string. After #pragma GCC pop_options, the macro must revert.
feature.root_cause_link: loongarch_pragma_target_parse did not update predefined macros after parsing the target attribute, so __loongarch_tune was not changed correctly.

source_features.root_cause_summary: loongarch_pragma_target_parse in loongarch-c.cc did not update predefined macros (like __loongarch_asx) after processing #pragma GCC target, so changes were not reflected until the fix.

feature.description: LoongArch64 ELF ABI (LP64D) where the hidden return pointer for large aggregates is passed in a general‑purpose register (e.g., a0 or a1), and the `setup_incoming_varargs` target hook must skip it when processing `...` arguments.
feature.root_cause_link: LoongArch’s `setup_incoming_varargs` initially did not advance past the hidden return pointer for `(...)` functions returning large structs; fixed in a backend patch.

source_features.root_cause_summary: On many targets, the `setup_incoming_varargs` hook did not advance past the hidden return pointer for C23 `(...)` functions returning large aggregates, causing `va_start/va_arg` to read the wrong registers.

feature.description: Integer constant multiplier in expressions of the form (unsigned_bitfield * CONST). Changing CONST from 37 to 36 avoids the ICE; 37 triggers the problematic optimization pattern. Vary the constant to explore similar crashes or missed optimizations.
feature.root_cause_link: The constant 37 leads to a specific factorisation (2*18+1?) that triggers the shift+mask pattern; the fix ensures the mask mode is sign-extended to DImode, eliminating the ICE.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In the LoongArch backend, loongarch_reassoc_shift_bitwise() was called with SImode while the constant mask operand was actually DImode, causing a wide-int mode mismatch and ICE in late_combine when trying to combine a shift+mask pattern with an addition for the alsl.w instruction.

feature.description: For LoongArch, stack protector combined set and test insns must not leave the canary value or its address in any general-purpose register after a stack-protected function returns.
feature.root_cause_link: The added stack_protect_combined_{set,test} patterns ensure sensitive data is not left in registers.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch backend lacked stack_protect_set/test patterns, causing SSP lowering to use generic emits that left the canary value in a register at function return.

group_summary: Combine five LoongArch-specific bugs into a single Fortran test source that, when compiled with different flag sets, triggers distinct ICEs or expected successful compilation. The source includes a WHERE construct (bug-123643), MERGE intrinsic (bug-115169), SIGN intrinsic (bug-118501), and integer-to-float vector bitwise operations via TRANSFER (bug-122097). The same source is also compiled with -flto to test bug-113233.
group_title: LoongArch SIMD ICEs and LTO with Fortran WHERE and vector operations
instantiation_constraints: The source must be a single Fortran file with no external dependencies.
All arrays must be of size a multiple of the SIMD width to ensure vectorization.
The MERGE intrinsic must use a scalar constant to trigger the const_int issue.
The TRANSFER-based bitwise operation must involve a constant integer mask to create a float vector constant.
SIGN must be applied elementally to arrays to generate vector xorsign.
Compilations must be done separately; the test driver must check for ICE or success accordingly.
notes: The group requires careful tuning of the Fortran source to ensure each bug is reliably triggered under its specific flags. The TRANSFER-based bitwise operation is the most fragile; if it does not reproduce bug-122097, alternative constructs like using the XOR intrinsic on integer vectors cast to real might be tried.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch backend lacked a pattern for vec_merge of a scalar zero duplicate in V4DF mode, leading to an unrecognizable insn during virtual register instantiation. This is likely the same issue as bug 117575, fixed by adding the missing pattern.

feature.root_cause_link: The unguarded call to REGNO on a const_int operand triggers the RTL checking assertion.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In loongarch_expand_conditional_move, REGNO was called on operands without checking REG_P, leading to an ICE when a constant integer (like const0_rtx) was used in a conditional move comparison.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch lacked TARGET_OPTION_SAVE/RESTORE and SWITCHABLE_TARGET, causing LTO to ignore per-object target options and SIMD builtins to be unavailable.

feature.description: This bug is specific to targets with non-bit-preserving floating-point loads, such as x86/x86_64 with x87 FPU (using -mfpmath=387 or in 32-bit mode). The fix introduces target hook TARGET_MODE_CAN_TRANSFER_BITS; for LoongArch, this hook currently returns true for all modes, but the test serves as a regression check for future changes.

source_features.root_cause_summary: SCC VN value-numbers a later integer load of a memory location as equivalent to a previous float load from the same location, but on x87 the float load (flds/fldl) converts sNaN to qNaN, so the bit pattern is not preserved. The fix prevents this value-numbering for modes where the target cannot transfer bits via a load.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Incorrect mapping of RTX comparison codes to vector FP compare mnemonics in LSX/LASX backend caused unordered comparisons to use 'cne' instead of 'cune', producing wrong results with NaN operands.

feature.description: The LoongArch cpymemsi expansion should handle remainders by successively halving the transfer mode size (e.g., from 8 bytes to 4 to 2 to 1) rather than falling back to byte mode immediately, to avoid excessive byte stores.
feature.root_cause_link: The fix introduces halving of mode size for remainders instead of falling back to byte mode at once.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch cpymemsi expansion generated inefficient inline code for memcpy of certain sizes under -mno-strict-align because it did not use wider modes when unaligned access was allowed, and improperly handled remainders by falling back to byte transfers. The fix improves alignment handling and uses a mode-halving strategy for leftovers.

feature.code_witness:
; Old pattern (before fix):
(define_insn "@indirect_jump<mode>"
  [(set (pc) (match_operand:P 0 "register_operand" "r"))]
  ""
  "jr\t%0"
  [(set_attr "type" "jump")
   (set_attr "mode" "none")])
; New pattern (after fix):
(define_insn "@indirect_jump<mode>"
  [(set (pc) (match_operand:P 0 "register_operand" "e"))]
  ""
  "jr\t%0"
  [(set_attr "type" "jump")
   (set_attr "mode" "none")])
feature.description: The LoongArch machine description patterns 'jumptable' and 'indirect_jump' must use the 'e' constraint (which excludes $ra and a few other registers) instead of 'r' (general registers) to prevent the use of $ra for indirect jumps.
feature.root_cause_link: Directly the fix commit 5430c86e71927492399129f3df80824c6c334ddf

source_features.root_cause_summary: Micro-architecture unconditionally treats 'jr $ra' as a return, causing branch prediction interference when $ra is used for non-return indirect jumps; fix was to restrict jump table and indirect jump patterns from using $ra via constraint 'e'.

feature.description: On LoongArch, registers $t0-$t8 are caller-saved. The compiler must not assume they retain their value across a function call without explicit save/restore.
mutation_knobs: additional local variables to increase register pressure
feature.root_cause_link: GCC assumed $t3 was callee-saved, but ABI says caller-saved.

source_features.root_cause_summary: GCC's LoongArch backend treated $t3 as callee-saved, violating the ABI; when a PLT stub clobbers $t3 in -fno-PIC -shared code, the register is corrupted across calls.

feature.description: A hot loop with high register pressure, mixing integer and floating-point operations, and containing conditional branches or conditional moves that use FCC registers.
feature.root_cause_link: This shape stresses register allocation and scheduling, and with incorrect pressure classes, the compiler might spill excessively or schedule poorly.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The rtx cost values defined by the LoongArch target backend influenced the default IRA register pressure class calculation, leading to poor scheduling decisions and performance degradation on LA664 cores. The fix provides explicit pressure classes (GENERAL_REGS, FP_REGS, FCC_REGS) to avoid the automatic calculation.

feature.description: A runtime check that a function calling __builtin_eh_return returns the expected value on a normal path; if the value is incorrect, the program aborts.
feature.root_cause_link: The overwritten return value causes the check to fail, leading to abort.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch epilogue unconditionally restored EH_RETURN_DATA_REGNO registers ($r4-$r7) on normal return paths, overwriting the function return value.

feature.description: The expander for atomic_exchange in loongarch/sync.md for modes smaller than SI used to generate a code sequence with a load and a compare-and-exchange loop, which is incorrect for an exchange because the store must be unconditional. The fix replaces it with a new define_insn that performs a conditional store via a loop that only exits after storing.
feature.root_cause_link: Directly corresponds to the root cause: the expander for atomic_exchange was using the wrong RTL pattern.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch backend expanded subword atomic_exchange into an incorrect load-cmpxchg sequence where the store could be skipped due to a concurrent write, fixed by introducing a dedicated exchange pattern that always completes the store.

feature.description: A function with a large stack frame (e.g., local array larger than the 12-bit signed immediate range of LoongArch's addi.d, i.e., >2047 bytes) forces the prologue to emit a stack tie insn to prevent instruction reordering around the stack adjustment.

source_features.root_cause_summary: match.pd folded fmin/fmax(sNaN, sNaN) to sNaN instead of qNaN; LoongArch backend used smin/smax RTL codes, also enabling wrong constant folding with -fsignaling-nans.

feature.description: A multithreaded program where two threads repeatedly perform atomic exchange on a shared subword variable, reading back their own previous values, and checking that the XOR of the three values is consistent. feature.root_cause_link: The failure oracle depends on the invariant that the XOR of the variable and the two thread-local copies remains constant; if exchanges are not atomic, the invariant breaks.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch backend expanded subword atomic_exchange into an incorrect load-cmpxchg sequence where the store could be skipped due to a concurrent write, fixed by introducing a dedicated exchange pattern that always completes the store.

feature.description: Compiling with -fno-PIC -shared on LoongArch causes the linker to generate PLT stubs that may use $t3 (and possibly other caller-saved registers). GCC must treat all calls under these options as clobbering all caller-saved registers.

source_features.root_cause_summary: GCC's LoongArch backend treated $t3 as callee-saved, violating the ABI; when a PLT stub clobbers $t3 in -fno-PIC -shared code, the register is corrupted across calls.

feature.description: On LoongArch, bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR) with an immediate should be performed before a left shift when the mask fits in an immediate operand, and either the shifted mask is expensive to load, or the shift amount allows further combination with an add instruction (e.g., alsl). source_features.root_cause_summary: GCC's target-independent canonicalization applies left shift before bitwise operations, forcing large constant loads on RISC targets. Target-specific reassociation can avoid expensive constants by swapping the order when the bitwise mask fits in an immediate.

feature.description: The RTL combiner pass invokes simplify_compare_const to perform narrowing of memory comparisons with constants. The optimization replaces a wider memory access with a narrower one when comparing against a constant that fits the narrower mode.
feature.root_cause_link: The bug resided inside simplify_compare_const, where the constant representation for the narrowed comparison was incorrectly generated.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In RTL combine's simplify_compare_const, when narrowing a memory comparison with a constant, the constant was emitted via GEN_INT instead of gen_int_mode, violating the invariant that constants in modes with fewer bits than HOST_WIDE_INT must be sign-extended. This caused an ICE in wide-int decomposition when the constant did not fit the expected form.

feature.root_cause_link: noce_try_shifted_store_flag was missing; the patch added this to replace conditional-zero sequences with shift+op patterns.

source_features.root_cause_summary: ifcvt.cc failed to generate conditional zero sequences when one operand is a CONST_INT, and lacked optimization for selects across A and A OP C where C is a power of two.

feature.description: LoongArch LSX store-only vector intrinsics (e.g., __lsx_vst) with a CVPOINTER parameter should not trigger -Wmaybe-uninitialized when the destination buffer is uninitialized, because the intrinsic only writes.
feature.root_cause_link: The builtin’s second parameter was CVPOINTER (const volatile void *) instead of VPOINTER (volatile void *). The const qualifier made GCC assume the memory could be read, causing the false positive.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch LSX/LASX store builtins used a const-qualified pointer (CVPOINTER), causing GCC’s -Wmaybe-uninitialized to treat the destination as potentially read even though the instruction only writes. This falsely warned when passing uninitialized memory.

group_summary: This group combines five missed optimization features into a single C test with two translation units. A shared struct S provides data for all patterns. Linking with -flto (bug-114978) enables interprocedural effects. Assembly scanning detects the optimizations.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The RTL combiner lacked target-specific splitters for LoongArch to convert the expression (a^b)^(a|c) into (c&~a)^b using the andn instruction, resulting in suboptimal code generation.

feature.description: In the generated assembly for the test function at -O3, there should be exactly one instruction sequence that computes the base address of the indexed struct element. Duplicate sequences (e.g., two LEA or two MUL for the same base) indicate a missed CSE.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Early combine pass avoids 2->2 combinations when the intermediate instruction is unchanged, preventing a zero-extension from being folded into multiple subsequent additions. The fix introduces a late-combine pass that handles such cases.

feature.code_witness: -g -Ofast -march=la464 -flto
feature.description: Link-time optimization (-flto) can amplify the regression because it enables more aggressive interprocedural optimization, potentially expanding more loops with uncertain trip counts, leading to more ADDRESS_REG_REG.
feature.root_cause_link: Report shows regression is often larger with -flto; LTO may expose more optimization opportunities that interact with the cost model.

source_features.root_cause_summary: A change in SCEV chrec_fold_multiply (commit e0e9499aeffd) altered loop analysis, causing suboptimal address selection on LoongArch. The RTL address cost for register+register addressing (ADDRESS_REG_REG) was too low (factor), leading to excessive complex addressing that increased register pressure and code size, degrading performance. Tentative fix increased cost to factor*3.

group_summary: Combines five LoongArch-specific features into a single C++ source file with shared global arrays and vector operations. The dot-product loop (bug-125474) writes to a global array, which is then used in a bitwise expression (bug-122431) and sorted with a problematic comparator (bug-113204). A LASX vector initialization (bug-117575) and a heap allocation (bug-106828) are included. source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch LSX/LASX store builtins used a const-qualified pointer (CVPOINTER), causing GCC’s -Wmaybe-uninitialized to treat the destination as potentially read even though the instruction only writes. This falsely warned when passing uninitialized memory.

feature.description: The bug is specific to LoongArch64 and requires frame pointer omission enabled (e.g., -fomit-frame-pointer or default at -O2). The rnreg pass (LoongArch register renaming) is active at -O2 and higher.
feature.root_cause_link: The fix ensures that when frame_pointer_needed is false, the stack tie references sp instead of fp, so this condition is the key target requirement.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The loongarch_emit_stack_tie function always emitted a stack tie referencing the hard frame pointer register ($fp/r22), even when frame_pointer_needed was false, causing regs_ever_live[$fp] to be set incorrectly. This misled the rnreg register renaming pass into using $fp as a target replacement register, potentially clobbering it without proper saving.

feature.description: LTO linking must preserve per-object target options for SIMD code generation. Compiling with -flto and -mlsx or -mlasx should produce binary code that uses the enabled SIMD instructions.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch lacked TARGET_OPTION_SAVE/RESTORE and SWITCHABLE_TARGET, causing LTO to ignore per-object target options and SIMD builtins to be unavailable.

dependencies.description: The boolean value (cast to int) from bug-112935 is used as operand 'a' in the identity expression of bug-96692.
The result of the identity expression is used as the carry_in for the carry chain of bug-110304 (via a glue feature).
The sum output of the carry chain is cast to signed _BitInt(513) and used as one operand in the _BitInt addition of bug-123635.
The asm barrier and noreturn call are placed after all other computations, serving as a termination point for the function.
Glue G1 provides the boolean value via a comparison, which is then cast and used in the identity.
Glue G2 passes the carry_in (derived from identity result) to the carry chain macro.

glue_features.novelty_rationale: Combines carry chain output with _BitInt widening, forcing the compiler to handle mixed widths and sign extensions while also checking the asm barrier termination.

group_summary: Combines five distinct GCC bugs into a single C program. The program computes values using the bitwise identity (a^b)^(a|c), verifies it matches (c&~a)^b. It also uses a boolean operand with a cast to trigger gimple_zero_one_valued_p. Includes an asm volatile barrier before a noreturn call (__builtin_unreachable) to test stack slot reuse. Uses _BitInt addition with sign extension to test zero padding. Emulates carry addition with __builtin_uadd_overflow and OR to test pattern matching. All values are checked via assertions for correctness, and the program compiles with -O2 -std=c23 targeting LoongArch.
group_title: LoongArch optimization and wrong-code test combining boolean cast, asm barrier, bitwise identity, _BitInt widening, and carry chain
instantiation_constraints: The program must be a single C file compiled with -O2 -std=c23.
Include <stdbool.h> and <stdint.h> for exact-width types if needed.
Define __builtin_uadd_overflow as available (GCC builtin).
All assertions must be static_assert or runtime assert to verify correctness.
The noreturn function can be __builtin_unreachable() after the asm barrier.
Use a small test framework to report success/failure.
notes: All features are preserved as independent invariants. Glue features connect them through data flow. The asm barrier is placed at the end as a terminator. The _BitInt addition uses values coming from earlier features. The test is self-checking via assertions.

must_not_change: The boolean operand must be computed via a comparison that yields 0/1 (e.g., (x==0) or similar).
There must be exactly one cast (e.g., (int)bool) that gimple_zero_one_valued_p looks through.
preservation_plan.placement: A boolean variable (0 or 1) is cast to int and used in an expression that the expander sees.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: The expand pass must use gimple_zero_one_valued_p on a boolean operand wrapped in a single-level cast. The operand is 0 or 1, and the cast preserves this property.

must_not_change: Do not remove or move the asm statement relative to the noreturn call.
Do not replace with a different barrier that might allow merging.
preservation_plan.placement: In the same function, after all computations, a call to a noreturn function is preceded by asm volatile("");
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: An empty asm volatile statement precedes a noreturn function call (or __builtin_unreachable) to prevent basic block merging.

must_not_change: Do not reorder operands or change operator precedence.
Do not simplify manually; the compiler must perform the optimization.
preservation_plan.placement: Compute both sides and assert equality. The expression must appear exactly as (a ^ b) ^ (a | c) with the same parentheses.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: The expression (a ^ b) ^ (a | c) is bitwise-equivalent to (c & ~a) ^ b. The compiler should generate code that matches this identity.

must_not_change: Do not cast away the signedness of the narrower operands.
preservation_plan.placement: Add two signed _BitInt(513) values and assign to an unsigned _BitInt(1025) variable. The upper bits must be zero.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: When a narrower signed _BitInt result is sign-extended and stored into a wider unsigned _BitInt, the padding limbs above the precision are zeroed (not sign-extended).

must_not_change: Do not replace with a single builtin or a different sequence.
The type used must be unsigned int (or as per the macro definition).
preservation_plan.placement: Compute a+b with carry using the macro pattern from the feature. The carry_out must be computed as (_c1 | _c2).
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Carry addition is emulated by two __builtin_uadd_overflow calls, with the carry output being the OR of the two overflow flags.

recommended_oracles: Correctness oracle: All computed values (identity equality, _BitInt result, carry sum) must match expected results.
Compilation oracle: Compiler must not crash or emit diagnostics beyond warnings.
Optimization oracle: Optionally check generated assembly for presence of andn instruction (for identity) and absence of extra zeroing (for _BitInt).

semantic_risks.mitigation: Use defined behavior: addition of two signed _BitInt values is defined in C23. The test will check the result explicitly.
semantic_risks.risk: The _BitInt widening may cause undefined behavior if padding bits are incorrectly interpreted; but the feature is about a compiler bug, so the test should expose it.

semantic_risks.mitigation: Place the asm barrier and noreturn call at the very end, after all computations, to minimize interference.
semantic_risks.risk: The asm barrier may affect optimization of other parts of the function; but that is the intended effect.

semantic_risks.mitigation: None needed.
semantic_risks.risk: Compiler options -O2 and -std=c23 are compatible; no conflict.

shared_execution_context.control_flow: Sequential execution with conditional assertions. The asm barrier and noreturn call are placed after all computations.
shared_execution_context.data_flow: Values from earlier computations (boolean cast result, identity result, carry sum) are used as operands in later features.
shared_execution_context.description: A single function that executes all patterns in sequence, with shared variables for inter-feature data flow.
shared_state: int a, b, c; unsigned carry; _BitInt(513) q, r; unsigned _BitInt(1025) i;

feature.code_witness:
bool bit0_p = gimple_zero_one_valued_p (treeop0, nullptr);
bool bit1_p = gimple_zero_one_valued_p (treeop1, nullptr);
feature.description: The expand pass should use gimple_zero_one_valued_p to identify boolean (0/1) valued operands because it handles a single level of cast, whereas tree_nonzero_bits may not have the necessary non-zero bit information set by earlier passes like phiopt4.
mutation_knobs: vary the presence of a cast on the boolean operand
test with and without phiopt4 enabled
feature.root_cause_link: After r14-1655, phiopt4 creates new SSA names without updating nonzero bits, so tree_nonzero_bits misses them; gimple_zero_one_valued_p looks through one extra cast.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The expander failed to recognize boolean (0/1) SSA names when wrapped in a cast, because tree_nonzero_bits does not look through casts. Additionally, the LoongArch cost model underestimated integer multiply cost, leading to poor instruction choices.

feature.description: Inserting an empty inline assembly statement `asm volatile("");` before a noreturn function call or __builtin_unreachable acts as a barrier that prevents optimization passes from merging the basic blocks, thereby allowing stack slot reuse.
mutation_knobs: position of asm relative to noreturn call
feature.root_cause_link: asm volatile prevents basic block merging, thus avoiding the liveness issue.

source_features.root_cause_summary: GCC's stack conflict analysis in add_scope_conflicts conservatively marks all variables live at the first instruction of a block, causing artificially enlarged liveness when noreturn calls from different codepaths are merged into a single basic block by optimization passes (tree-pre, code-hoisting), preventing stack slot reuse.

feature.description: The expression (X ^ Y) ^ (X | Z) is bitwise-equivalent to (Z & ~X) ^ Y.
mutation_knobs: apply to other integer widths (short, long, unsigned)
use bitwise NOT instead of XOR: (a ^ b) ^ (~a & c)
feature.root_cause_link: This identity is the basis for the optimization that requires target support for andn.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The RTL combiner lacked target-specific splitters for LoongArch to convert the expression (a^b)^(a|c) into (c&~a)^b using the andn instruction, resulting in suboptimal code generation.

feature.description: Separate extension case: when a narrower signed _BitInt result is sign-extended and stored into a wider unsigned _BitInt, the padding limbs above the precision must be zeroed (not sign-extended), while limbs within the precision are correctly sign-extended.
feature.root_cause_link: In lower_mergeable_stmt, the separate_ext handling failed to zero the limbs beyond precision when sign-extending into an unsigned wider type.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The _BitInt lowering pass (gimple-lower-bitint.cc) did not handle targets that specify padding bits must be sign- or zero-extended, especially when the ABI limb precision exceeds the internal limb precision, leading to missing stores for padding limbs and wrong-code.

feature.code_witness:
#define __builtin_addc(a,b,carry_in,carry_out) \
  ({ unsigned _s; \
     unsigned _c1 = __builtin_uadd_overflow (a, b, &_s); \
     unsigned _c2 = __builtin_uadd_overflow (_s, carry_in, &_s); \
     *(carry_out) = (_c1 | _c2); \
     _s; })
feature.description: Carry addition emulated by two __builtin_uadd_overflow calls with OR of carry outputs
mutation_knobs: replace OR with ADD when carry-in is known 0/1
use narrow integer types (unsigned char, unsigned short)
vary the order of the two overflow checks
feature.root_cause_link: The commit r14-1837 added pattern matching for this exact sequence, but initially missed 8/16-bit variants and sub-borrow.

source_features.root_cause_summary: GCC update r14-1837 added pattern matching for carry-add operations using __builtin_uadd_overflow, but did not include support for 8-bit/16-bit carry builtins (__builtin_adcb, __builtin_subcb) or carry-sub (__builtin_subcl) patterns on architectures without hardware carry flags like LoongArch, resulting in missing compiler builtins and suboptimal code for carry-chain arithmetic.

group_summary: Combines five GCC bugs on LoongArch: reload infinite loop (113148), wrong-code due to vec_perm aliasing (121064), LRA matching constraint ICE (87600), combine narrowing constant sign-extension ICE (110939), and ext-dce sign-extension removal wrong-code (116915). All bugs are triggered via a single test program that shares global state and data flow, requiring -O2 on LoongArch.
group_title: LoongArch reload, combine, ext-dce, and wrong-code bug cluster
instantiation_constraints: Test must be compiled with -O2 on a LoongArch target (e.g., loongarch64).
Register variables in bar() must be assigned to hard registers REG1 and REG2 that are different; macros or explicit register names required.
Buffer for dotprod must be initialized as per bug 121064: buffer[0]=-1, buffer[1]=1, rest zero.
Volatile keyword used to prevent optimizations that might avoid memory comparison or store.
Float variables in test_reload should be sufficiently many to cause register pressure.
notes: The group integrates five diverse bugs into a single test, forcing interaction via data flow and register pressure. The output of the asm function is used to seed the dotprod computation, whose result subsequently influences comparisons and stores that trigger the other bugs. This creates a rich interdependence not present in individual test cases.

must_not_change: The function must not use explicit asm to fix registers; must rely on register allocation to create pseudos without hard registers.
preservation_plan.placement: A function test_reload() with multiple double variables and a comparison (e.g., if (a < b)) to cause register pressure and trigger secondary reload.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: The loongarch_secondary_reload function must correctly handle FCCmode operands that are pseudo-registers with true_regnum == -1, not just MEM_P.

must_not_change: Function signature and algorithm unchanged; buffer must be initialized as per original bug.
preservation_plan.placement: As a separate function definition.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Function long_filter_ehigh_3830_1 must return -1 for input buffer={-1,1} and all-zero initial arrays; otherwise __builtin_trap.

preservation_plan.placement: A separate function bar() that is called before other tests.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: ASM code shape with two hard register variables, one earlyclobber output, and matching constraint.

must_not_change: The comparison must be between a memory operand and a constant; the constant must be representable in a narrower mode.
preservation_plan.placement: A function test_combine() that performs a volatile memory read and compares with a small constant (e.g., 5) to trigger combine simplification.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: Combine must not produce a CONST_INT that violates mode precision invariant when narrowing a memory comparison with a constant.

must_not_change: The store must involve a narrow signed type (e.g., signed char) and a wider destination, not using casts that widen before store.
preservation_plan.placement: A function test_extdce() that stores a signed char value into a long long pointer, forcing sign extension.
preservation_plan.preserved_invariant: ext-dce must not remove a SIGN_EXTEND when storing a narrow signed value into a wider memory location.

recommended_oracles: Compilation should succeed without ICE; if ICE occurs, test fails.
Runtime: if __builtin_trap is reached, test fails (wrong-code detected).
Alternatively, compare output of main returning 0 vs unmodified.

feature.description: Reload pass infinite loop when loongarch_secondary_reload for FCCmode fails to detect a memory operand because it only checks MEM_P, ignoring pseudo-registers not yet assigned a hard register (true_regnum == -1).
mutation_knobs: alter register pressure to change pseudo allocation
feature.root_cause_link: Direct cause of infinite reload: missing regno == -1 check.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch secondary reload for FCCmode assumed MEM_P(x) was sufficient to detect memory operands, missing cases where x is a pseudo-register not yet assigned a hard register (true_regnum(x)==-1). This caused infinite reload instructions and an ICE with 'maximum number of generated reload insns per insn achieved'.

mutation_knobs: use __builtin_printf to observe output vs. trap
feature.root_cause_link: With the alias bug, the vectorized permutation produces wrong intermediate values, causing final dotprod to be wrong (e.g., 8 instead of -1).

source_features.root_cause_summary: The TARGET_VECTORIZE_VEC_PERM_CONST expansion on LoongArch allowed the target pseudo-register to alias an input operand, so loading the selector into d->target clobbered the input, causing wrong-code for vshuf instructions.

feature.description: Function with two local register variables assigned to different hard registers, used in asm with "=&r" output and matching constraint "1".
feature.root_cause_link: The LRA constraints handling must correctly handle matching constraints with hard registers.

source_features.root_cause_summary: An IRA fix (non_conflicting_reg_copy_p) incorrectly allowed overlapping pseudos, which reload could not handle, causing wrong-code; also combine propagating hard regs into asm caused LRA earlyclobber conflicts; a later LRA fix for user hard register reloads resolved LoongArch ICE.

feature.description: When narrowing a memory comparison with a constant, the constant must be sign-extended to the precision of the narrower mode. The RTL combiner must maintain the invariant that CONST_INT values in modes with fewer bits than HOST_WIDE_INT are sign-extended representations of the original constant.
feature.root_cause_link: The ICE occurred because a CONST_INT was created with bits beyond the mode's precision, violating the normal form for narrow constants.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In RTL combine's simplify_compare_const, when narrowing a memory comparison with a constant, the constant was emitted via GEN_INT instead of gen_int_mode, violating the invariant that constants in modes with fewer bits than HOST_WIDE_INT must be sign-extended. This caused an ICE in wide-int decomposition when the constant did not fit the expected form.

feature.code_witness: /* ext-dce must not remove the SIGN_EXTEND in: (set (mem:DI (reg:DI ptr)) (sign_extend:DI (subreg:SI (reg:DI ...)))) */
feature.description: The ext-dce pass must call carry_backpropagate before stripping extensions, so that SIGN_EXTEND and ZERO_EXTEND operations are visible and their sign bits can be marked live; otherwise, the pass may incorrectly eliminate these extensions when the source is a narrow signed value and the destination is a wider memory location.
mutation_knobs: sizes of source and destination modes
feature.root_cause_link: The fix moved carry_backpropagate call before stripping extensions and added handling for SIGN_EXTEND and ZERO_EXTEND in that function.

source_features.root_cause_summary: ext-dce pass called carry_backpropagate after stripping extensions, causing SIGN_EXTEND bits not to be marked live, leading to wrong elimination of sign extensions and incorrect code.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In gimple-lower-bitint, when shortening large INTEGER_CST PHI arguments, the minimal precision was rounded up to a multiple of limb_prec but on targets where abi_limb_mode > limb_mode (e.g., aarch64 TImode vs DImode), the stored constant had padding limbs that were incorrectly zero instead of extended bits (ones). feature.description: fold_truth_andor in fold-const.cc may transform a logical OR into a bitwise OR based on LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT, but later dojump.cc may undo that transformation back to short‑circuit branches based on BRANCH_COST, creating inconsistent decisions.
feature.root_cause_link: The confusion between LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT and BRANCH_COST leads to suboptimal code when the two decisions clash, especially on targets like LoongArch.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT macro is inconsistently used across optimization passes and may conflict with BRANCH_COST checks in dojump.cc, leading to missed optimizations for targets like LoongArch that define it as 0.

feature.description: A chain of floating-point comparisons joined by logical OR in a conditional branch, with all operands loaded from memory via pointer, triggers premature non-short-circuit conversion.
feature.root_cause_link: The code shape triggers the LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT early folding, which does not consider the cost of individual comparisons.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The middle-end fold-const/ifcombine pass prematurely converts logical OR of comparisons into non-short-circuit form without considering target comparison cost, leading to missed-optimization on targets where LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT is enabled.

feature.code_witness: long foo(long a, long b, long c, long d) { return a || b || c || d; }
feature.description: Verify that at -O2, a logical OR chain of integer comparisons produces assembly with minimal branches and uses conditional sets/moves when the target supports cheap operations. An oracle can scan for the number of branch instructions in the generated assembly and flag if it exceeds a threshold.
feature.root_cause_link: With default LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT, the compiler should optimize this chain to use conditional sets; with the macro set to 0, it may produce branches, which is a regression for integer code.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The RISC-V port incorrectly defined LOGICAL_OP_NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT=0, likely inherited from MIPS, causing missed optimizations for logical expressions with cheap conditional sets; fixed by removing the macro to use the default.

feature.description: Zero extension of a smaller integer to a wider integer, when the extended value is used in multiple arithmetic operations, must be folded into the using instructions so that no separate zero-extension instruction appears.
mutation_knobs: arithmetic op (add, sub, mul, and, or, xor)
feature.root_cause_link: Early combine failed due to 2->2 restriction; late-combine substitutes definition into all uses.

source_features.root_cause_summary: Early combine pass avoids 2->2 combinations when the intermediate instruction is unchanged, preventing a zero-extension from being folded into multiple subsequent additions. The fix introduces a late-combine pass that handles such cases.

feature.description: Interaction between SCEV analysis (chrec_fold_multiply) and RTL address selection: a change in SCEV overflow handling can cause loops to be expanded differently, leading to more ADDRESS_REG_REG insns, which become harmful when the cost model underestimates them.
mutation_knobs: trip count values that might overflow in SCEV
feature.root_cause_link: Commit e0e9499aeffd is the trigger; it changed chrec_fold_multiply, which then exposed the latent cost model issue.

source_features.root_cause_summary: A change in SCEV chrec_fold_multiply (commit e0e9499aeffd) altered loop analysis, causing suboptimal address selection on LoongArch. The RTL address cost for register+register addressing (ADDRESS_REG_REG) was too low (factor), leading to excessive complex addressing that increased register pressure and code size, degrading performance. Tentative fix increased cost to factor*3.

conflicts: Feature 1 requires a missing libm function causing link failure, while features 2 and 3 require successful linking and execution. The test is designed so that link failure (expected on LoongArch) tests feature 1, and if linking succeeds (on other targets), the runtime checks test features 2 and 3. This yields a non-deterministic per-target outcome but respects all invariants.

feature.description: Targets that lack a standard 'nans' function in their default libm (e.g., LoongArch, possibly others) are more likely to exhibit the incorrect call, because the fallback to the library function is expected to fail at link time.

feature.description: The miscompilation causes a function that computes a total order on floating-point numbers (using bit-level comparison) to return an incorrect result when comparing a signaling NaN (SNaN) with a quiet NaN (QNaN). The oracle is a test that aborts if the result is wrong.

feature.root_cause_link: The wrong-code occurs because the integer loads of x and y retrieve the converted (qNaN) values instead of the original sNaN, causing the bit comparison to fail.

source_features.root_cause_summary: SCC VN value-numbers a later integer load of a memory location as equivalent to a previous float load from the same location, but on x87 the float load (flds/fldl) converts sNaN to qNaN, so the bit pattern is not preserved. The fix prevents this value-numbering for modes where the target cannot transfer bits via a load.

feature.description: A vector load after a scalar store to overlapping memory must observe the stored value.
feature.root_cause_link: Missing memory operand in RTL caused the scheduler to reorder load before store.

source_features.root_cause_summary: LoongArch LSX/LASX vldx/xvldx builtins were defined using unspec without (mem) in RTL, causing the instruction scheduler to reorder them with stores.

feature.code_witness: Examples: 0x80000000 (high bit set), 0xFFFFFFFF (all bits set), 0x7FFFFFFF (below high bit), for narrow mode 32-bit. For 16-bit narrow mode: 0x8000, 0xFFFF, 0x7FFF.
feature.description: Constant values that are unsigned and have the most significant bit set in the target narrow mode (e.g., 0x80000000 for a 32-bit narrow mode on a 64-bit host) are crucial for exposing the sign-extension mishandling. Varying the constant around the sign boundary can stress the fix.
feature.root_cause_link: The sign-extension bug only manifests for constants that change representation when sign-extended, i.e., unsigned with high bit set in the narrow mode.

source_features.root_cause_summary: In RTL combine's simplify_compare_const, when narrowing a memory comparison with a constant, the constant was emitted via GEN_INT instead of gen_int_mode, violating the invariant that constants in modes with fewer bits than HOST_WIDE_INT must be sign-extended. This caused an ICE in wide-int decomposition when the constant did not fit the expected form.

feature.description: The bug only manifests on LoongArch64 when compiling with -O2, which enables sibling call optimization. The register $r13 (t1) is used as a temporary in the epilogue, so it must be excluded from SIBCALL_REGS.
feature.root_cause_link: The target-specific use of $r13 in epilogue and sibcall creates the conflict.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The LoongArch epilogue uses $r13 as a temporary register (LARCH_PROLOGUE_TEMP), but $r13 was included in SIBCALL_REGS, allowing it to be allocated for sibling call targets. When a sibcall was followed by the epilogue, the target address in $r13 was clobbered, causing a jump to an invalid address.

feature.root_cause_link: The flag was introduced to allow backends to differentiate, as part of the fix.

source_features.root_cause_summary: A change in the C++ FE stopped removing zero-width bitfields after layout, exposing them to backends. This caused ABI mismatches between C and C++ for parameter passing on several targets. The fix introduced a DECL_FIELD_CXX_ZERO_WIDTH_BIT_FIELD flag so backends can decide to ignore or warn about such bitfields.

source_features.root_cause_summary: The initial conversion of loops to EXECUTE_IF_SET_IN_HARD_REG_SET in r17-1279 incorrectly passed a temporary (abi.full_reg_clobbers()) to the macro, causing undefined behavior when the temporary's lifetime ended, leading to miscompilation and bootstrap failures on multiple targets.
